page: Microsoft Azure M48bds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine driven by the Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at up to 4.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with two threads per core. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced acceleration features including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8 instruction sets.

The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU allocation ratio. Local storage is provided through a 429 GB local SSD disk, supporting temporary files and fast swap spaces alongside Premium Storage capabilities. The instance operates without discrete GPUs and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on virtual network routing for external connectivity.

Benchmark measurements place memory bandwidth in the top tier, achieving 3,658.62 GB/sec on small cached blocks and 214.01 GB/sec on large uncached read transfers, paired with 92.37 GB/sec for uncached writes. General computing metrics reflect strong multi-core performance, scoring 19,030.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 59,487.53 in PassMark CPU tests. The integrated AMX instructions also support CPU-based inference workloads, delivering 28.89 tokens per second on medium 7B parameter models.

This hardware profile delivers substantial computational density and memory capacity, avoiding the overhead of specialized GPU accelerators. It is best suited for enterprise relational databases, large in-memory caches, software compilation clusters, and heavy multi-threaded data processing pipelines.
